column1: # Known test failures — the executable ledger.
# lane <TAB> file <TAB> test name <TAB> signature
# READ ci/lib/known_failures.py BEFORE ADDING A ROW. The short version:
#   * A registered test still asserts the CORRECT behaviour and still fails.
#     Never edit a test to match today's wrong answer — that teaches the next
#     maintainer that the wrong answer is the contract, which is the whole
#     reason this file exists rather than a `skip`.
#   * A registered test that starts PASSING fails the lane by name. That is the
#     signal. Delete its row; do not "resolve" it in place.
#   * `signature` is a substring that must appear in THAT case's own failure
#     output. It is what stops an entry from silently absorbing a different
#     failure of the same test — a ledger keyed on identity alone has already
#     green-lit a failure nobody reviewed, in a sibling repo, when a schema bump
#     made a journey throw on its first line.
#   * The failing set must equal the registered set exactly, so a new red is
#     never absorbed by its neighbours, and a suite that never ran (compile
#     error, crash before the first case) can never be excused by its rows.
# Registering is the LAST resort. If the product can be fixed cheaply, fix it:
# `new_trace_caption_chrome_test.nim`'s red was going to be registered here and
# turned out to be a grep that had not followed its subject to another module,
# so it was fixed instead and has no row.
# THE STRICT MOCK, 2026-09-02.
# `MockBackendService.send` now validates against `VALID_DAP_COMMANDS` and
# raises. That turned eleven silently-wrong dispatches into honest reds. The
# full triage is `src/frontend/viewmodel/backend/dap_dialect.md` §7b; the short
# form is that all eleven send a command NO ENGINE IMPLEMENTS, so the tests are
# right and the product is wrong.
# These are NOT "adding the string to VALID_DAP_COMMANDS" jobs. That list
# describes what the engine implements; editing it implements nothing.
#   ct/load-recent-trace, ct/load-recent-folder, ct/new-record, ct/launch-config
#     FIXED 2026-09-02; all 18 rows (9 cases x 2 lanes) removed.
#     Wrong transport, not a wrong name — an Electron IPC channel, a
#     main-process concern the replay engine should never implement.
#     This entry used to say "a host-callback seam on WelcomeScreenVM (it has
#     none at all) plus host wiring — four seams". That was wrong, and wrong in
#     an expensive direction: it priced the fix as new construction. The seam
#     existed. `WelcomeScreenCallbacks`
#     (`viewmodel/views/isonim_welcome_screen_view.nim`) already declared
#     `onRecentTraceClick` / `onRecentFolderClick` / `onSubmitNewRecord`,
#     `buildWelcomeCallbacks` (`ui/welcome_screen.nim`) already filled them with
#     the live `CODETRACER::...` sends, and the view already PREFERRED them,
#     falling back to the VM only when a callback was nil. It sat on the VIEW's
#     callbacks record rather than on the VM's type — which is exactly why an
#     inspection that read the VM declaration and stopped concluded there was
#     no seam anywhere.
#     What it actually took: four `proc` fields on `WelcomeScreenVM` following
#     the `errors_vm.nim` pattern already landed for `ct/jump-location`,
#     `installWelcomeVMCallbacks` in `ui/welcome_screen.nim` assigning the
#     closures that already existed, and one adapter for the single genuine
#     mismatch — `launchSelectedConfig` is keyed by `slug` while
#     `CODETRACER::record-with-launch-config` is keyed by `configIndex`
#     (`index/traces.nim`), so the request carries the entry's position in the
#     list the host itself installed.
#     Note the four commands remain ABSENT from `VALID_DAP_COMMANDS`, and
#     `dap_dialect.md` §7's nine are still nine: the fix was to stop sending
#     them, not to bless them. `test_mock_backend_validates_dap_commands.nim`
#     still rejects all nine with its count asserted.
#   ct/load-step-lines
#     Genuinely dead. No engine arm loads step lines for a location and there is
#     no analogue to redirect to, so there is nothing to rename it to either.
#     Retired by: an engine command for it.
# Both files run in vm-native (C) and vm-js (node), so each case is registered
# for both lanes: the defect is in the ViewModel, which is backend-neutral.
vm-native
